tasks.summary: 22 implementation tasks across setup, shared Twitch API groundwork, three independently testable user-story phases, and cross-cutting validation; P1 catalog/mapping and redemption handling precede P2 operational recovery.

T001.did: Documented Twitch OAuth setup, callback and required redemption scope, admin reward mapping, and the difference between authorization and live processing.

T002.did: Added a server-side Twitch Helix client with request timeouts, sanitized errors, authenticated broadcaster lookup, paginated reward listing, and EventSub subscription creation.

T003.did: Added mocked HTTP coverage for Twitch reward listing, disconnected state, safe provider failures, public response fields, and token isolation; added SQLite reopen persistence coverage.

T004.did: Added passing validation cases for duplicate reward IDs, partial-map collisions, valid action names, and empty disabled assignments.

T005.did: Added frontend contract assertions for the catalog refresh control, reward selectors, duplicate feedback, availability metadata, and independent authorization/live account status.

T006.did: OAuth now verifies the broadcaster identity with Twitch before storing tokens, persists ID/login with encrypted-token metadata, and exposes only safe identity/status fields.

T007.did: Implemented paginated Helix reward retrieval with reward IDs, current titles, costs, enabled/user-input state, and no title-based matching.

T008.did: Wired the Helix client into the app and added the authenticated reward endpoint with disconnected responses, bounded/sanitized errors, and reauthorization status on expired or under-scoped tokens.

T009.did: Server-side reward mapping now rejects duplicate non-empty IDs across actions while preserving empty values for disabled actions.

T010.did: Replaced manual ID entry with reward selectors and refresh controls, displayed availability and cost, preserved unavailable mappings, and blocked duplicate assignments.

T011.did: Added offline EventSub WebSocket tests for welcome/subscription setup, redemption notification validation, keepalive, session reconnect handoff, invalid payloads, and bounded retry lifecycle.

T012.did: Engine tests verify exact Twitch reward-ID mapping, Twitch user ID priority over login fallback, no action for unmatched viewers, and persisted redemption-ID deduplication.

T013.did: Implemented Twitch EventSub WebSocket session handling for redemption subscription, validated notifications, keepalive, session handoff, retry limits, revocation, and safe transport errors.

T014.did: Wired EventSub redemption events through the existing RewardService and shared Socket.IO broadcast path, with sessions and subscriptions scoped to the stored broadcaster identity.

T015.did: RewardService accepts Twitch EventSub redemption fields, keeps idempotent redemption insertion and scene mutations transactional, and relies on the existing unique redemption ID constraint.

T016.did: Added offline lifecycle tests for authorized-but-not-live status, retry/recovery, subscription revocation, logout cleanup, graceful server shutdown, and DonationAlerts isolation.

T017.did: Standardized Twitch authorization and live statuses to the specified enums, retained only public broadcaster identity, and enforced allowed state values at the status boundary.

T018.did: Added bounded exponential reconnection, subscription restoration for fresh sessions, retry/error/listening transitions, and retry termination on invalid auth or revocation.

T019.did: Wired listener start after OAuth/startup, stop-before-local-logout cleanup, disconnected startup status, and graceful shutdown of EventSub plus Socket.IO/HTTP without mutating DonationAlerts.

T020.did: The admin cards now display broadcaster account, Twitch authorization and live states separately, preserve DonationAlerts, and present provider-authored recovery guidance.

T021.did: Updated setup and operation docs for the exact Twitch callback/scope, UI-based mappings, distinct live/auth statuses, bounded recovery, logout isolation, and offline checks without Twitch credentials.

T022.did: Full offline test suite passed (26/26); backend entry-point checks, syntax checks for changed Twitch backend modules, and the admin browser module syntax check all passed.
